key_insight: This study suggests antenatal iron-folic acid non-initiation and short duration are related but distinct gaps in Nigeria, with no antenatal contact being the strongest driver of non-initiation.
clinical_relevance: The findings can help target maternal health outreach and ANC access efforts to improve iron-folic acid coverage and reduce anemia risk in pregnancy.
method: Cross-sectional secondary analysis of NDHS 2023–24 women aged 15–49
Modeled two outcomes: non-initiation and <90-day use among initiators
Compared survey-weighted logistic regression with elastic net, random forest, and XGBoost
evidence_signal: Using an 80:20 held-out test split, XGBoost showed the best discrimination for both outcomes (AUC 0.922 for non-initiation and 0.721 for short duration), outperforming survey-weighted logistic regression.
watch_item: Because this is observational survey data, associations may not prove causation and self-reported supplementation status may be affected by recall or reporting bias.
paper_title: Antenatal Iron-Folic Acid Supplementation Gaps in Nigeria: A Predictive Machine Learning Analysis of Non-Initiation and Sub-Optimal Duration Using NDHS 2023-24
